messages.content: Write an engineering team's year in review post for an internal blog. Around 250 words.

output:
**Draft — 2026 in review** (numbers and names are placeholders; swap in your real ones)

---

### The year, roughly

We started January with a deploy pipeline that took 41 minutes and we're ending it with one that takes six. That's the change I'd point to first, because everything else got easier once we stopped waiting on it.

The migration off the monolith took three quarters instead of two. Nobody's fault — the billing tables were more tangled than the design doc admitted, and we spent most of Q2 untangling them before a single service moved. Worth it. Checkout p95 went from 900ms to 310ms.

Some numbers: 1,247 PRs merged. Four incidents at Sev-2 or worse, down from eleven. On-call went from six people to nine, which is the quiet reason that second number moved.

What didn't happen: the feature-flag cleanup. We have 340 dead flags in the codebase and I have personally pushed that ticket four times. The docs rewrite stalled in March. If you were counting on either, I'm sorry. Both are on the Q1 list and this time they have an owner.

Two people joined (welcome, Priya and Sam) and one left. Marcus — thank you for the seven years.

What I want for next year is boring: fewer things in flight. We ran five parallel initiatives and finished three. Three initiatives, finished, would have felt better and cost less.

See you Monday.

---

~250 words. To make it yours, the parts that carry the most weight are the failure paragraph and the number you lead with — pick the metric your team actually complained about in standup.
